query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Create customized application emails with resume and cover letter PDFs, stage them as Outlook drafts, update attachments and body text, then send the finalized drafts after confirmation.
query_ground_truth.query: create outlook email drafts with body text and attachments
query_ground_truth.intent: Stage the generated PDFs and customized text as drafts within Outlook.

results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Step]: Create a draft using OUTLOOK_CREATE_DRAFT (set body as HTML with is_html=true; ensure to_recipients is populated; optionally include small attachments at creation; store message_id).

[Optional (if attachments are needed)] [Step]: Add each attachment using OUTLOOK_ADD_MAIL_ATTACHMENT (reuse message_id; use a tool-accessible file reference or valid contentBytes; for inline images set isInline=true and set contentId to match the HTML cid).

[Optional (if OUTLOOK_ADD_MAIL_ATTACHMENT fails or files are large)] [Fallback]: Upload via OUTLOOK_CREATE_ATTACHMENT_UPLOAD_SESSION (reuse message_id; follow uploadUrl/nextExpectedRanges until the attachment is committed).
[Optional (for verification before leaving as draft)] [Next Step]: Retrieve the draft using OUTLOOK_GET_MESSAGE (confirm recipients, body contentType/content, and hasAttachments).
[Optional (if edits are needed after review)] [Next Step]: Update the existing draft using OUTLOOK_UPDATE_EMAIL (reuse message_id; keep HTML cid references stable if inline items exist).
[Required (only after user confirmation)] [Step]: Send the finalized draft using OUTLOOK_SEND_DRAFT (use the final message_id).
known_pitfalls: [OUTLOOK_CREATE_DRAFT] Using the wrong recipient field (not to_recipients) can create a draft with no usable To recipients.
[OUTLOOK_GET_MESSAGE] Retrieved HTML may be normalized/wrapped; validate rendering if formatting must be exact.
[OUTLOOK_ADD_MAIL_ATTACHMENT] May fail with 403-style behavior if the attachment reference is not accessible to the tool runtime.

[OUTLOOK_ADD_MAIL_ATTACHMENT] Bad Request/HTTP 400 can occur when contentBytes is not valid base64 or the attachment payload shape cannot be deserialized; inline images also break if contentId doesn’t match the HTML cid.
[OUTLOOK_CREATE_ATTACHMENT_UPLOAD_SESSION] Attachment appears only after upload completes; respect nextExpectedRanges/uploadUrl semantics and exact total size.

OUTLOOK_CREATE_DRAFT.description: Creates a new Outlook email draft with subject, body, recipients, and an optional attachment. This action creates a standalone draft for new conversations. To create a draft reply to an existing conversation/message, use the OUTLOOK_CREATE_DRAFT_REPLY action instead.

attachment.description: Optional file(s) to attach. Accepts a single file or a list of files.

cc_recipients.description: Optional list of CC (carbon copy) recipient email addresses. Must be provided as an array of strings, e.g., ["cc@example.com"].

to_recipients.description: Optional list of primary 'To' recipient email addresses. Must be provided as an array of strings, e.g., ["user@example.com"] for a single recipient or ["user1@example.com", "user2@example.com"] for multiple recipients. Do not pass as a JSON-encoded string. Can be omitted when creating a draft to be completed later. To send the draft, at least one valid address must be present across `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, or `bcc_recipients`.

bcc_recipients.description: Optional list of BCC (blind carbon copy) recipient email addresses. Must be provided as an array of strings, e.g., ["bcc@example.com"].

OUTLOOK_ADD_MAIL_ATTACHMENT.description: Tool to add an attachment to an email message. Use when you have a message ID and need to attach a small (<3 MB) file or reference.

item.description: Embedded item (e.g., message, event) for itemAttachment; must include its own '@odata.type'.

name.description: Display name of the attachment (e.g., file name). Required when using content_bytes. When using the attachment field, the name is automatically inferred.

user_id.description: The user's principal name or 'me' for the authenticated user.

isInline.description: Set to true if the attachment should appear inline in the message body.

contentId.description: Content ID for inline attachments, used in HTML body references.

name.description: The filename that will be used when uploading the file to the destination service

s3key.description: The S3 key of a publicly accessible file, typically returned from a previous download action that stored the file in S3. This key references an existing file that can be uploaded to another service.

mimetype.description: The MIME type of the file

attachment.description: File to attach to the email. Either provide this field OR use 'content_bytes'. Cannot be used together with 'content_bytes'.

message_id.description: Unique Microsoft Graph message ID (opaque string like 'AAMkAGI2TAAA='). NOT an email address - this is an internal identifier returned by Microsoft Graph API operations.

odata_type.description: The OData type of the attachment. Required by Microsoft Graph API. Use '#microsoft.graph.fileAttachment' for file attachments, '#microsoft.graph.itemAttachment' for embedded items (messages, events, contacts).

contentType.description: MIME type of the attachment (e.g., 'application/pdf'). Required when using content_bytes. When using the attachment field, the mimetype is automatically inferred.

contentBytes.description: Base64-encoded content of the file attachment (max size 3 MB). Either provide this field OR use the 'attachment' field (recommended). Cannot be used together with 'attachment'.

contentLocation.description: URL location or path for reference attachments.

OUTLOOK_LIST_OUTLOOK_ATTACHMENTS.description: Lists metadata (name, size, contentType, isInline — but not `contentBytes`) for all attachments of a specified Outlook email message. Returns fileAttachment, itemAttachment, and referenceAttachment types; only fileAttachment entries support download via OUTLOOK_DOWNLOAD_OUTLOOK_ATTACHMENT. Results include inline images and signatures — filter by `isInline == false` and check `contentType` to identify real document attachments. Results are nested under `data.response_data.value`.

user_id.description: The unique identifier of the user. Use the user's UPN (e.g., 'AdeleV@contoso.onmicrosoft.com') or 'me' for the currently authenticated user. This specifies the mailbox to query.

message_id.description: The unique identifier of the email message from which to retrieve attachments. Must be a message ID (obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_MESSAGES or OUTLOOK_SEARCH_EMAILS), not a folder ID or calendar event ID. Folder IDs look similar but will cause an error. When sourcing from OUTLOOK_SEARCH_EMAILS, use `hitId` as the message identifier — not `resource.id`.

response_detail.description: Level of detail in the response. 'minimal' (default) returns only the attachment metadata that exists on the Graph attachment base type (id, name, size, contentType, isInline, lastModifiedDateTime) — the base64-encoded contentBytes and any fileAttachment-only fields (contentId, contentLocation) are excluded so the heavy file payload never leaves Microsoft Graph. 'full' returns the complete payload including contentBytes for downloading.
